blurTest.evidence: At gallery scale the contestant input card, mode selector, and large circular picker remain the unmistakable dominant objects.

silhouetteTest.evidence: The oversized NameSnap wordmark, single list-building card, and circular picker create a product-specific silhouette unlike the browser, authenticator, and remote-control utility references.

fiveSecondTest.evidence: A fresh install opens directly to an empty field labeled Contestant List with the explicit action Add These Names to Pool.

realityTest.evidence: The launch state contains no sample contestants or mock winner history; counters are zero and the picker is visibly inactive.

journeyTest.evidence: The first screen exposes the real input-to-pool-to-spin workflow immediately, and the existing stateful picker remains intact.

platformTest.evidence: Fresh-install renders on the dedicated iPhone 17 Pro simulator respect the safe area, native controls, scrolling, and both standard and Accessibility Dynamic Type.

buyerValueTest.evidence: The app delivers its paid and free value on launch instead of delaying the name-picking task behind instructional screens.

implementationTest.evidence: The onboarding branch and persistence key were deleted, build 13 compiles, and fresh-install simulator launches consistently render ContentView.

screenFindings: Current Utilities references from Google Chrome, Google Authenticator, and TV Remote reinforced the category rule that a single-purpose utility should expose its working object and safest next action immediately.
The launch state is truthful and empty: no mock contestants, winner history, or seeded settings appear.
At extreme Dynamic Type the branded title remains on one line and the complete primary input card stays legible and unobstructed.
Marketing-frame conventions from the reference corpus were not imported into the canonical app interface.
repairs: Removed the three-screen onboarding branch and its stored completion flag so every launch enters ContentView directly.
Capped the dense workspace at the first Accessibility Dynamic Type tier and allowed the wordmark to scale down on one line after the initial extreme-size render wrapped and obscured content.
Hidden Reset This Pool and Clear This Pool until a pool exists so irrelevant destructive controls no longer cover the empty first-use workspace.
verdict: Approved after standard-size, gallery-scale, original-resolution, and Accessibility Dynamic Type renders on a fresh install. The launch path now goes directly to the real empty name-picker workspace with no onboarding or critical visual failure.
